# `⍠` — Axis

Dyadic operator. Keys: `Alt-q ;`. Hanzi: `轴` (`軸`)

`f⍠A` applies `f` to the cells made of the axes `A`. The other axes form the frame. `A` is an axis or a vector of axes, given as numbers or names. Axes count from 0, and negative axes count from the end. A record operand gives options, which [Fill](#fill) describes.

```bpl
m←2 3ρι6ₓ
+/⍠0 m                    ⍝ [3 5 7]ₓ
ax←0 ◇ +/⍠ax m            ⍝ [3 5 7]ₓ
```

Numeric [subscripts](../scripts.ipynb#subscripts) give literal axes: `+/₀` is `+/⍠0`, and `+/₁ ₂` is `+/⍠[1 2]`. Use `⍠` for names, computed axes and options records.

`⌽₀` reverses the first axis; `⌽₋₁` reverses the last, as plain `⌽` does. A nonnegative axis that the data lacks adds trailing length-1 axes, as [views](../terms.qmd#term-view), before `f` applies. With axis 1, shape `[2]` is treated as `[2 1]`. This holds for every `f`:

```bpl
10 20 ,₁ 30 40            ⍝ [10 30◇20 40]
2#₁10 20                  ⍝ [10 10◇20 20]
2↑₁10 20                  ⍝ [10 0◇20 0]
```

Negative axes select only existing axes. With two arguments, no axes are added when the higher-rank argument has the selected axes. Counts and selectors, such as `2` in `2#₁10 20`, keep their ordinary meaning. On an atom, axis 0 first makes a length-1 vector.

[Rank](jot-diaeresis.qmd) selects the last `r` axes: `⍤1` is `⍠¯1`.

```bpl
m←2 3ρι6ₓ
+/⍤1 m                    ⍝ [3 12]ₓ
+/⍠¯1 m                   ⍝ [3 12]ₓ
+/⍠0 m                    ⍝ [3 5 7]ₓ
```

Result cells with the same rank as the selected cells return to the axes `A`. Other result cells start at the first selected axis.

```bpl
m←2 3ρι6ₓ
⌽⍠0 m                     ⍝ [3 4 5◇0 1 2]ₓ
ρ,⍠0 1⁝2 3 4ρι24ₓ        ⍝ [6 4]ₓ
```

With two arguments, `A` applies to both. Cells pair using leading agreement of the frames, as for [Rank](jot-diaeresis.qmd). An argument without the selected axes is one cell, paired with every cell of the other.

```bpl
m←2 3ρι6ₓ
1 0 1 #⍠1 m               ⍝ [0 2◇3 5]ₓ
10 20 +⍠0 m               ⍝ [10 11 12◇23 24 25]
```

A string selects one axis by name, and a vector of strings several. A [named index](iota.qmd) (`ι["row":2]`) or an index from [`•index`](../system/index.qmd) selects its own axis.

```bpl
n←["row":2 "col":3]ρι6ₓ
+/⍠"row" n                ⍝ ["col":3]ρ[3 5 7]ₓ
+/⍠"row" "col" n          ⍝ 15ₓ
r←ι["row":2] ◇ +/⍠r n     ⍝ ["col":3]ρ[3 5 7]ₓ
[b k]←•index 2 3 ◇ +/⍠k b+k   ⍝ 3 6
```

A function right operand computes the axes from the arguments: `f⍠g Y` is `f⍠(g Y) Y`, and `X f⍠g Y` is `X f⍠(X g Y) Y`. [Rank](jot-diaeresis.qmd) and [Stencil](quad-diamond.qmd) take a function right operand in the same way. Here `g` selects the longest axis:

```bpl
m←2 3ρι6ₓ ◇ +/⍠{↑⍒ρω} m      ⍝ [3 12]ₓ
```

## Exceptions

For these primitives, `⍠A` has another meaning:

- Multi-axis Reduce, including seeded Reduce. `+/⍠1 2` flattens each cell before reducing.
- Partitioned Enclose and Partition. `1 0 1 0⊂⍠1` and `1 1 2 2⊆⍠1` cut the whole matrix into blocks along axis 1. `⊂⍠K` matches Dyalog. Dyalog's `⊆[K]` partitions each vector along axis `K` instead, which is `{α⊆ω}⍠K` here.
- Rotate with a count array. `1 2 3 4⌽⍠0` pairs one count with each column.
- Mix. `⊃⍠A` places the assembled cell axes among the frame axes; it does not extend the nested input's axes.
- Axis selectors. `ι⍠A` returns the keys or positions of the selected axes.

```bpl
+/⍠1 2⁝2 3 4ρι24ₓ        ⍝ [66 210]ₓ
```

Wrapping a primitive in a dfn gives the general rule:

```bpl
{+/ω}⍠1 2⁝2 3 4ρι24ₓ     ⍝ [6 22 38◇54 70 86]ₓ
m←2 4ρι8
1 1 2 2{α⊆ω}⍠1 m        ⍝ [[0 1] [2 3]◇[4 5] [6 7]]
```

## Inverse

`f⁻⍠A` inverts `f` along the same axes. Arithmetic and math functions, comparisons, Rotate, Replicate, the catenates, Enclose, Split, Mix and Reverse have such inverses.

```bpl
10 20+⁻⍠0[11 12 13◇24 25 26]   ⍝ [1 2 3◇4 5 6]
```

## Fill

The operand can be an options record, as in `f⍠["fill":v]`. The record has one option: `fill` gives the item for each filled position, in place of the array's [prototype](../terms.qmd#term-prototype). Fill applies to: pervasive calls, keys one argument lacks; Take, past the end; Replicate, negative counts; Expand, inserted items; Mix, padding; Index and Pick, positions outside the axis or not whole; Pick and First, position 0 or ¯1 of an empty axis; Reshape, an empty argument. It applies too when `f` has a bound argument (`3↑`) or an axis (`↑⍠1`, `↑⍠{0}`). In `(f⍠R1)⍠R2`, `R1`'s fill applies. Any other function raises DOMAIN.

```bpl
a←["p" "q"]:1 2 ◇ b←["q" "r"]:3 4
a+b                             ⍝ ["p":1 "q":5 "r":4]
a+⍠["fill":10] b                ⍝ ["p":11 "q":5 "r":14]
5↑⍠["fill":¯1] 1 2 3            ⍝ 1 2 3 ¯1 ¯1
⊃⍠["fill":$n] [[1 2] [3]]         ⍝ [1 2◇3 $n]
[[$n 1]]⌷⍠["fill":¯1] 10 20 30  ⍝ ¯1 20
(3↑⍠1)⍠["fill":¯1] [1 2◇3 4]    ⍝ [1 2 ¯1◇3 4 ¯1]
(3↑⍠{0})⍠["fill":¯1] [1 2◇3 4]  ⍝ [1 2◇3 4◇¯1 ¯1]
((3↑)⍠["fill":¯1])⍠["fill":¯2] 1 ⍝ 1 ¯1 ¯1
```

The fill is converted to the data's type, and never changes the result's type. A float fill is rounded to the data's float width. Integers, Booleans, characters: the type must hold the fill's value exactly. Under dynamic kinds, ordinary integers are widened to fit a whole fill. A nested array accepts any fill.

```bpl
5↑⍠["fill":255] [1 2 3]ₓ₁      ⍝ [1 2 3 255 255]ₓ₁
5↑⍠["fill":¯1000] [1 2 3]ₓ     ⍝ [1 2 3 ¯1000 ¯1000]ₓ
3↑⍠["fill":"NA"] "a" "bc"      ⍝ "a" "bc" "NA"
```

The fill is checked when the call starts, even if no position is filled, against every argument that could be filled (pervasive: those with a keyed axis). [Windows](up-down-arrow.qmd) and [Stencil](quad-diamond.qmd) take a `fill` key in their own options records. A fill given to them through `⍠` raises DOMAIN.

## Errors

- `RANK`: an axis operand that is not a unit or vector
- `DOMAIN`: axes that aren't whole, repeated axes, negative axes outside the higher-rank argument, an options record with a key other than `fill`, a function that fills no position, Windows or Stencil, or a fill that doesn't keep its value as the data's type
